newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees 1998 start for new meat authority.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees 1998 start for new meat authority.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it was aiming to have a single meat corporation replacing the red meat industry's three main statutory bodies to be in operation by January 1998.

"I expect legislation to be approved by around November this year. This will allow a possible start-up date for the new arrangements of January 1998," Primary Industries Minister John Anderson told a meat industry conference.

Under the new structure announced last month, separate operating units will be responsible for jointly funded research and development, food safety and quality. There would also be separately managed operating units for beef and sheepmeat marketing and promotion.

Anderson said he would not agree to reducing levies or winding up the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp or the Meat Research Corp until he was satisfied there would be no interruption to functions and staff resources the industry would like to see continue.

He said the Ausmeat industry standards authority would undoubtedly continue probably as a joint venture between producers, processors, lot feeders, livestock exporters and pig and goat meat interests.
"The continuation of overseas representation might also attract varying levels of interest between the various sectors, depending on their particular concerns," Anderson said.
Changes to the industry structure followed a major government review of the red meat industry which presented the adopted structure as a minority recommendation.
Statutory levies on processors and livestock exporters would be set to zero but could be reimposed if insufficient funds were raised to meet agreed activities
"I expect people to deliver on the commitments they have given me. We will go back to compulsory levies if it (voluntary levy) does not work," Anderson said in his speech.
Anderson said the government was also addressing the reform of the Australian Quarantine Inspection Service (AQUIS) "in particular the matter of meat inspection."
Emphasis was also being placed on food safety initiatives and wider market access for Australian meat products, he said.
